project.title: calendar-buddy
overview: calendar-buddy is a lightweight, fast calendar application for Linux, connected directly to Google Calendar. It replaces opening Google Calendar in the browser for everyday calendar work. It is built for the product owner's own use, with the option of sharing it with colleagues, and runs without a server of its own: the data stays in Google and in a local cache.

goals.text: For two consecutive working weeks, the product owner checks upcoming meetings, responds to invitations and creates meetings with Google Meet only in the app, without opening Google Calendar in the browser.
goals.raw: - G1: For two consecutive working weeks, the product owner checks upcoming meetings, responds to invitations and creates meetings with Google Meet only in the app, without opening Google Calendar in the browser. (`SRC-01-04`, `SRC-01-129`, `DEC-05`, `DEC-48`)

head: Actor
Who they are
How they sign in
Access, in short
rows: A person using the app on their own Linux computer with one or more of their own Google accounts (personal or Workspace) — for now the product owner, later possibly colleagues
Google account through the system browser (OAuth); no password in the app
Their own calendars and those shared with their accounts, within Google's permissions; on each event they act as organizer or guest

head: Term
Means exactly
rows: A Google account (personal or Workspace) connected to the app.
A Google calendar accessible to a connected account, including read-only and subscribed ones.
An account's main calendar; invitations land there, and on a Workspace account only there can special event types be created.
The calendar, chosen by the user, that new events go to.
A calendar whose events are temporarily hidden by the quick toggle; it stays listed and keeps synchronizing.
A calendar turned off in the settings; it is not listed, not synchronized and gives no reminders.
A calendar whose notifications are off; its events stay visible.
A single entry in a Google calendar.
A recurring event / one of its instances.
The reach of a change to a series: *this event*, *this and following*, or *all*.
The person who invites to an event / an invited person, required or optional.
An event in which the user is a guest.
A per-user Google reminder on an event, as a notification or an e-mail, synchronized with Google.
The desktop notification the app shows for a notification-type reminder.
The local copy of calendar data, from one year back to two years ahead.
No network; only what is in the cache can be browsed.
Guests' busy blocks for the chosen day, shown in the event editor.
Opening the Google Meet meeting of an event from the event, the agenda or a notification.

topics.title: Product, roles, platform and integrations
topics.scope: What the product is and for whom (the single end user, product framing, the "replace the browser" goal), the Google integration strategy (Calendar API, People API, OAuth verification), the provider abstraction and future providers, the target platforms, and the preliminary stack (see SRC-01 *Noted*: §10.1, §10.2, §15, §16). Ends where a business topic describes behaviour. Project-level questions with no other home (acceptance, milestones, support) live here.

topics.title: Visual direction and themes
topics.scope: The look and feel: the Morgen and Apple Calendar references, light and dark themes following the system, restrained use of calendar colours, no unnecessary animation, and keyboard shortcuts as listed with themes in the MVP scope. Advanced theming is out. May merge into DSC-05 at /og:modules.

findings.text: The look combines the clarity and simplicity of Apple Calendar with the density and clear grid of Morgen.
findings.raw: - [DSC-06-01] The look combines the clarity and simplicity of Apple Calendar with the density and clear grid of Morgen. (`SRC-01-02`, `SRC-01-49`, `SRC-01-50`)

findings.text: The app has a light and a dark theme and can follow the system setting.
findings.raw: - [DSC-06-02] The app has a light and a dark theme and can follow the system setting. (`SRC-01-51`, `SRC-01-107`)

findings.text: Calendar colours help tell calendars apart, while the rest of the interface stays restrained.
findings.raw: - [DSC-06-03] Calendar colours help tell calendars apart, while the rest of the interface stays restrained. (`SRC-01-52`)

findings.text: There are no unnecessary animations and no features unrelated to the calendar.
findings.raw: - [DSC-06-04] There are no unnecessary animations and no features unrelated to the calendar. (`SRC-01-53`)

findings.text: The interface is in English only; adding translations later stays possible.
findings.raw: - [DSC-06-05] The interface is in English only; adding translations later stays possible. (`SRC-02-41`) — *source: `DEC-31`*

findings.text: There are no mock-ups; the look is refined on the working app, with the product owner reviewing it as it grows.
findings.raw: - [DSC-06-06] There are no mock-ups; the look is refined on the working app, with the product owner reviewing it as it grows. (`SRC-02-42`) — *source: `DEC-32`*

topics.title: Creating and editing events
topics.scope: Creating events (click/select, quick entry, full editor, fields, all-day and multi-day, recurrence), editing, deleting, dragging and resizing, moving between calendars, recurring instances and series, warnings and permission failures. Guests, RSVP and Meet are DSC-08; reminders are DSC-09.

findings.text: An event is created by clicking in the calendar or selecting a time range.
findings.raw: - [DSC-07-01] An event is created by clicking in the calendar or selecting a time range. (`SRC-01-54`)

findings.text: There is a quick way to add the essentials and a full event editor.
findings.raw: - [DSC-07-02] There is a quick way to add the essentials and a full event editor. (`SRC-01-55`)

findings.text: An event has a title, description, start and end, time zone and calendar; it can be all-day or span several days.
findings.raw: - [DSC-07-03] An event has a title, description, start and end, time zone and calendar; it can be all-day or span several days. (`SRC-01-56`, `SRC-01-57`)

findings.text: Where Google allows it, the location, reminders, busy/free status and visibility can be set.
findings.raw: - [DSC-07-04] Where Google allows it, the location, reminders, busy/free status and visibility can be set. (`SRC-01-58`)

findings.text: A new event goes to the calendar the user chose as the default; for a given event another calendar can be picked from a list grouped by account.

findings.text: Events can be edited and deleted within the user's permissions; the time is changed by dragging and the length by resizing.
findings.raw: - [DSC-07-06] Events can be edited and deleted within the user's permissions; the time is changed by dragging and the length by resizing. (`SRC-01-61`, `SRC-01-62`, `SRC-01-100`, `SRC-01-124`)

findings.text: An event can be moved to another calendar where Google allows it.
findings.raw: - [DSC-07-07] An event can be moved to another calendar where Google allows it. (`SRC-01-63`)

topics.title: Guests, invitations, RSVP and Google Meet
topics.scope: Inviting attendees (by e-mail, from contacts, directory and recent addresses), showing their status, required/optional guests, sending updates, responding to invitations (Accept/Decline/Maybe), organizer vs. attendee permissions, and adding or opening a Google Meet link.

topics.title: Reminders and notifications
topics.scope: Desktop notifications for upcoming events: honouring event reminders, turning notifications on and off, no duplicates, opening the event from a notification, and what happens when the app is closed.

findings.raw: - [DSC-09-01] Upcoming events are shown as system notifications. (`SRC-01-80`, `SRC-01-105`, `SRC-01-127`)

findings.raw: - [DSC-09-03] Each reminder gives one notification; synchronization never repeats it. (`SRC-01-83`)
